prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: construction-minded bowl and transition reference for a painterly Japanese seaside skating game, wide 3:2. A clean sculpted concrete skate bowl on an elevated pier terrace overlooking calm blue sea. High oblique view shows the entire open bowl interior and perimeter deck clearly. The bowl is generous, roughly 32 by 28 metres, a rounded rectangle with big flowing corners, broad flat bottom and smooth continuously curved quarter-circle walls rising 3 metres from bottom to coping. Walls become genuinely vertical at the lip, with a short vertical section; these are UP-AND-BACK transitions for aerials landing in the same wall, not shallow ramps that launch skaters forward. Smooth tangent floor-to-wall joins, silver steel coping with only subtle protrusion, narrow terracotta tile band below the lip. Pale warm ivory floor, muted sage transition walls, sand-coloured coping deck at least 3m wide. Bottom rests above the sea; the outer bowl terrace stands above the main pier and is reached by wide long mellow banks with smooth run-ins. Beside it show a smaller opposing-quarter-pipe mini-ramp with wide flat and a gentle entry bank, as a separate progression area. Minimal dark bronze safety rail at the OUTER terrace edge well behind the coping, never across a skating line. Sparse timber benches, coastal grass planters and a simple timber pergola stay beyond landing zones. Hand-crafted low-poly architectural game render, soft matte materials, warm afternoon shadows, beautiful quiet Japanese seaside setting. Keep it a clear practical geometry reference, no people hiding the surface, no water in bowl, no pits below waterline, no graffiti, no text, no UI, no random disconnected ramps.
